svg.title: How #63350 and #63351 make room for a voice turn
svg.desc: Panel a: a caller's speech goes to speech to text, then to vLLM 0.32's scheduler, which carries #63350 and #63351, then to text to speech and back to the caller; 24 coding-agent sessions send their requests to the same scheduler at priority 2, the voice turn's at priority 0; the scheduler allocates from the KV pool beneath it. Panel b, the KV preemption, #63350: in a pool of 12 KV blocks, two agent requests hold 5 each and 2 are free, fewer than the 4 a waiting voice turn needs; on vLLM 0.32 the turn keeps waiting, while the KV preemption preempts the latest agent request, agent B, and the turn takes 4 of its blocks. Panel c, the budget cap, #63351: the engine's steps in time, one box a step, from the reply's first token: on vLLM 0.32 each step of the reply also carries an agent's prefill chunk, so in the time the budget cap gives the reply its first 48 tokens the reply gets 14 without it; after the window, agent prefill resumes. Blocks and steps are illustrative.
